City Council Regular Meeting
Public Comment from the Audience
•
If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a Speaker Request Card, as it must be handed to the City Clerk before the start of the meeting.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on matters not listed on the agenda during the Public Comments from the Audience period.
•
Opportunity to address the City Council (on non-agenda items) is limited to 3 minutes per speaker.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote.
Brown Act
Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.
Rules of Decorum
Persons attending the meeting shall observe rules of propriety, decorum, good conduct, and refrain from impertinent or slanderous remarks. Violation of this rule shall result in such persons being barred from further audience before the governing body. Pursuant to Gov. Code Sect. 54954.3(c), any person who engages in unlawful interference shall be removed from chambers.
Americans with Disabilities Act
In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact the City Clerk's office at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to allow the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to the meeting or service.
This agenda was posted 72 hours in advance of the meeting at the City Hall, 8838 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; the L.A. County Library, Rosemead Branch, 8800 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; and other locations pursuant to RMC Sec. 1.08.020. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the Rosemead City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be made available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours.

C.
Request to Add and Proclaim “California Mosquito Awareness Week” and “National Police Week” to the Approved List of Proclamations for Year 2026
The San Gabriel Valley Mosquito and Vector Control District and the Los Angeles County Temple Sheriff’s Station have each requested that the City Council issue proclamations in support of their respective causes. The San Gabriel Valley Mosquito and Vector Control District is requesting a proclamation declaring April 13–19, 2026, as “Mosquito Awareness Week”, and the Los Angeles County Temple Sheriff’s Station is requesting a proclamation declaring May 10–16, 2026, as “National
Police Week”.
Recommendation: That the City Council approve the requests to add the “California Mosquito Awareness Week”, April 13-19 and the “National Police Week”, May 10-16 to the Approved Proclamations list for 2026 and schedule the presentations to a subsequent City Council meeting.
Staff Report
D.
Accept Completed Improvements and Authorize the Filing of a Notice of Completion for the City Hall Interior Renovations Project No. 31027
On November 12, 2024, the City Council awarded a construction contract to MLC Constructors, Inc. for the City Hall Interior Renovations Project. The total construction budget, including a 10% contingency, was $1,504,607.50. All construction improvements have been completed and have been accepted by the City Staff. A notice of completion will be filed with the Los Angeles County Recorder upon approval by the City Council. The release of retention funds will take place upon the filing of the notice of completion.
Recommendation: That the City Council take the following actions:
1.
Accept the completed improvements for the City Hall Interior Renovation Project No. 31027 as performed by MLC Constructors, Inc.; and
2.
Authorize the recordation of Notice of Completion with the Los Angeles County Recorder and the release of retention funds.
Staff Report
E.
Schedule a City Council Special Meeting for April 21, 2026, and Cancel the Regular Scheduled Meeting of April 28, 2026
On March 10, 2026, the City Council directed City staff to schedule a special meeting for Tuesday, April 21 at 7:00 p.m. as part of the required second public hearing
for the proposed charter item in lieu of the regularly scheduled meeting for
April 28, 2026.
Recommendation: That the City Council schedule a special meeting for Tuesday, April 21 at 7:00 p.m. to conduct the required second public hearing for the proposed charter item, in lieu of the regularly scheduled meeting and cancel the meeting of April 28, 2026.
Staff Report
F.
Termination of License Agreement with SiFi Networks Rosemead LLC
On January 10, 2023, the City entered into a License Agreement with SiFi Networks Rosemead LLC ("SiFi") for the design, construction, and operation of a fiber optic network within the public right-of-way. Since execution of the Agreement, SiFi has not met key contractual milestones, including submission of complete design plans and commencement of construction. Following multiple discussions and written correspondence, the City issued a formal Notice of Default. SiFi has not cured the identified deficiencies within the required timeframe and has instead requested substantial extensions to the Agreement schedule.
Recommendation: That the City Council take the following actions:
1.
Find that SiFi Networks Rosemead LLC is in material breach of the License Agreement dated January 10, 2023; and
2.
Authorize the City Manager to terminate the Agreement pursuant to Section 8 of the Agreement.
Staff Report
G.
Award of Contract for Professional Information Technology Management Services
The current Information Technology service contract will terminate on April 30th. Per the Rosemead Municipal Code section 3.24.090, using alternative purchasing procedures, staff sourced two top-ranking proposals from the year 2024 Request for Proposal, staff is recommending the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute a Professional Services Agreement with Acorn Technology Services for a
3-year contract in the total amount of $550,463 from April 27, 2026 – April 26, 2029, with an option for two one-year extensions.
Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute a 3-year Professional Services Agreement in the total amount of $550,463 from
April 27, 2026 – April 26, 2029, with Acorn Technology Services for Information Technology Management Services, including an option to renew for two one-year extensions.
Staff Report

Fiscal Year 2025-26 Mid-Year Budget Review
On June 10, 2025, the City Council adopted the 2025-26 Operating and Capital Improvement Program Budgets. This report summarizes the City’s General Fund overall financial position for the current fiscal year through December 2025 including a discussion on revenue sources and expenditure trends. The estimates stated within are just that, estimates, and are subject to change as the current fiscal year continues.
Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the Mid-Year Budget Review Report.
